title: The sync push gate judges a pushed range by its tip, so a commit that adds a leak-scan shape and a later one that removes it passes the gate and then blocks publish for good
goal: kbgit.py sync --push refuses a range up..HEAD in which any commit adds a leak-scan hit (the verdict publish gives each commit, kbpublic.leak_verdicts with the allowlist of the commit and of HEAD), naming the commit and the file and never the value, even when a later commit of the range removes the hit; a range with no such commit pushes as before

run:
import os, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile
def sh(*a, cwd=None, env=None):
    return subprocess.run(a, cwd=cwd, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True)
t = tempfile.mkdtemp()
c, o = t + "/c", t + "/o.git"
os.mkdir(c)
tar = subprocess.run(["git", "archive", "HEAD"], capture_output=True, check=True).stdout
subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", c], input=tar, check=True)
env = dict(os.environ, KB_SYNC_NO_TESTS="1", GIT_AUTHOR_NAME="t", GIT_AUTHOR_EMAIL="t@example.com", GIT_COMMITTER_NAME="t", GIT_COMMITTER_EMAIL="t@example.com")
for cmd in (["init", "-q", "-b", "main"], ["add", "-A"], ["commit", "-q", "-m", "base", "--no-verify"]):
    sh("git", *cmd, cwd=c, env=env)
sh("git", "init", "-q", "--bare", o)
sh("git", "fetch", "-q", c, "main:main", cwd=o)
for cmd in (["remote", "add", "origin", o], ["fetch", "-q", "origin"], ["branch", "-q", "--set-upstream-to=origin/main", "main"]):
    sh("git", *cmd, cwd=c, env=env)
d = c + "/kb/_self/backlog"
name = sorted(x for x in os.listdir(d) if x.endswith(".json"))[0]
path, iid = d + "/" + name, name[:-5]
with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
    clean = f.read()
home = "/".join(("", "Users", "realperson", "docs"))
bad = clean.replace("\"goal\": \"", "\"goal\": \"" + home + " ", 1)
for text in (bad, clean):
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write(text)
    sh("git", "commit", "-q", "-am", "chore(backlog): plant\n\nKB-Work: " + iid, "--no-verify", cwd=c, env=env)
tip = sh("git", "rev-parse", "origin/main", cwd=c, env=env).stdout.strip()
look = sh(sys.executable, "-I", "-c", "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, \"_tools\"); import kbpublic as k; print(k.history_refusals(\"HEAD\", sys.argv[1], k.tree_files(\"HEAD\", \".\"), \".\")[1])", tip, cwd=c, env=env)
r = sh(sys.executable, "_tools/kbgit.py", "sync", "--push", cwd=c, env=env)
refused = r.returncode != 0 and "leak" in (r.stdout + r.stderr).lower()
print("publish check of the range:", look.stdout.strip()[:140])
print("sync --push exit", r.returncode, "| refused for a leak:", refused)
shutil.rmtree(t, ignore_errors=True)
sys.exit(0 if refused else 1)

notes: Premise (run 2026-10-26 on a planted clone): commit bc14f216937a filed BG-23wnhrgc and d8609788f9 reworded it 18 s later; both were pushed in one sync, whose gate (backlog.py check, tests.py) reads the pushed tip's tree only, so it passed; kbgit.py publish scans the lines each commit adds against its parent (kbpublic.history_refusals, leak_verdicts) and refuses bc14f216937a for good, which stops every newer commit reaching the public home. The scan did not widen: kbcommon.LEAK_HOME is unchanged since 2026-09-28. Fix shape: the gate gets a range check beside check-trailers (kg_sync.gate, up..HEAD) that calls the publish verdict code, not a second implementation; it runs in every clone (cheap: only added lines, verdicts cached under _cache/publish/), not only where kb.publishRemote is set. Test: a push gate and a leak guard are critical (kb/_self/code.md), so one planted case goes into an existing scenario (test_sync_e2e.py), no new file or test id, within _tools/tests_ceiling.json, never a raise. No claim or coord note on _tools/kg_sync.py or _tools/kbpublic.py at planning (backlog.py held, coord digest). Related: ST-w6vnsox3 unblocks the commit already on main; BG-zexhpoqi stops the usual source.
